description: Rockers were a young, working-class youth subculture that emerged in the United Kingdom during the 1950s and flourished in the early to mid-1960s. The identity was defined by an appreciation for 1950s American rock and roll music and a passion for customizing and racing British café racer motorcycles. Known alternately as " Leather Boys " for their attire or " Ton-Up Boys " for their practice of riding at speeds over 100 mph ("doing the ton"), the Rockers cultivated a rebellious, masculine identity that stood in opposition to mainstream British society and, most famously, in direct conflict with their rivals, the Mods .
culturalContext: Key values (per the Aesthetics Wiki): Masculinity, rebellion, speed, group loyalty, 1950s rock and roll music
